{"artifact":"SmeDossierEnvelope","schema_version":"0.4.0","stage_id":"02.dossier_sections","probe":"rdmv-ct-d","lineage":{"input_manifest_sha256":"5c5e8db5472729f99ee8b19a463b341d515e70e2248bf160f549d6cc20cdff24","candidate_lineage_id":"2026-10-28-rdmv-ct-class-d:lineage:19","source_registry_sha256":"07bbe76598f0084cdb2ee450c7050097675dacd13ccc4c40045c307297557e80","source_liveness_sha256":"8fea57e2daef73f0a94408791d2027c4fc2c9799e8d48060efecbf84d96aedf5"},"envelope_scope":{"kind":"partial_chunk","assigned_section_ids":["C"],"chunk_index":1,"chunk_total":1},"section_char_limit":12000,"sections":[{"section_id":"C","chunk_id":"C.01","merge_seq":1,"domain":"Space cushion and maneuvers","heading":"C — Space cushion and maneuvers","learner_facing":true,"markdown":"## C — Space cushion and maneuvers

FACT_ID: sec05-F01 | anchor: A22
Spare trucks their braking room ahead, ease off to help their passes without ever speeding up, and hug right past oncoming rigs against wind shove. [A22]
Source: [A22 -> src:rdmv-ct-d:connecticut-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0022]
FACT_ID: sec05-F02 | anchor: A22
Trail trucks by at least three counted thousands to a roadside mark, since closer means driving blind to them and for them. [A22]
Source: [A22 -> src:rdmv-ct-d:connecticut-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0022]
FACT_ID: sec05-F03 | anchor: A22
Peeking left invites head on surprises, truck cleared debris still bites, rigs can outbrake cars, night high beams blind their mirrors, and upgrade stops need offset room against rollbacks. [A22]
Source: [A22 -> src:rdmv-ct-d:connecticut-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0022]
FACT_ID: sec05-F04 | anchor: A22
Long rear wheels cut corners short, forcing trucks left before right bends, so never slip up a turning truck right side toward the curb. [A22]
Source: [A22 -> src:rdmv-ct-d:connecticut-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0022]
FACT_ID: sec05-F05 | anchor: A22
Halt and gift backing trucks their swing room instead of circling around into invisibility and a needless crash. [A22]
Source: [A22 -> src:rdmv-ct-d:connecticut-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0022]
FACT_ID: sec05-F06 | anchor: A22
Honor truck slows and signals with patience, feed entering ramp traffic real gaps, and join highways through true openings without sweeping every lane. [A22]
Source: [A22 -> src:rdmv-ct-d:connecticut-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0022]
FACT_ID: sec05-F07 | anchor: A22
Grant stopping trucks their rail crossings, cruise right on narrower roads, favor center lanes amid heavy merges, and shun shoulders always. [A22]
Source: [A22 -> src:rdmv-ct-d:connecticut-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0022]
FACT_ID: sec05-F08 | anchor: A22
Join traffic at its own speed with full ramp run ups, never halting ramp ends, and brake early on ramps when gaps force waiting. [A22]
Source: [A22 -> src:rdmv-ct-d:connecticut-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0022]
FACT_ID: sec05-F09 | anchor: A22
Every merge wants a four second hole split two and two, and undersized holes only shrink further. [A22]
Source: [A22 -> src:rdmv-ct-d:connecticut-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0022]
FACT_ID: sec05-F10 | anchor: A23
Match surrounding pace because speed gaps breed crashes and passing gambles, while speeding banks just minutes per hour. [A23]
Source: [A23 -> src:rdmv-ct-d:connecticut-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0023]
FACT_ID: sec05-F11 | anchor: A23
Hold main road pace until exit ramps, and brake late then briskly yet safely for fast two lane turnoffs with followers behind. [A23]
Source: [A23 -> src:rdmv-ct-d:connecticut-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0023]
FACT_ID: sec05-F12 | anchor: A23
Cross only through full clear widths, pause solely in fitting medians, keep left paths and greens truly open under ticket threat, trust no blinker until it turns, and never halt atop rails. [A23]
Source: [A23 -> src:rdmv-ct-d:connecticut-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0023]
FACT_ID: sec05-F13 | anchor: A23
Gauge gaps by thousands from a fixed mark: arriving before three means tailing, so fall back and recount until three holds. [A23]
Source: [A23 -> src:rdmv-ct-d:connecticut-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0023]
FACT_ID: sec05-F14 | anchor: A23
Stretch to four seconds on slick roads, for passing neighbors, behind motorcycles, unseen tailers, trailers, dim sight, emergency rigs, halt bound crossings and hill stops, and cede right to tailgaters. [A23]
Source: [A23 -> src:rdmv-ct-d:connecticut-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0023]
FACT_ID: sec05-F15 | anchor: A24
Guard rear room with steady pace and early signals, park pickups off road, telegraph parallel moves, yield slow lanes at turnouts, mirror every slowdown, and melt right or ease gently for tailgaters, never brake checking. [A24]
Source: [A24 -> src:rdmv-ct-d:connecticut-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0024]
FACT_ID: sec05-F16 | anchor: A24
Own side room by shunning packs, centering lanes, sliding over for joiners, padding parked cars, granting walkers and wheels full adjoining lanes with three bike feet, splitting hazards toward trucks, and sequencing threats singly. [A24]
Source: [A24 -> src:rdmv-ct-d:connecticut-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0024]
FACT_ID: sec05-F17 | anchor: A24
Shun blind spots beside and behind others by speeding clear or dropping back, sprint through passing blind zones, and never cruise beside big rigs. [A24]
Source: [A24 -> src:rdmv-ct-d:connecticut-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0024]
FACT_ID: sec05-F18 | anchor: A24
Slow through malls, rush crushes, tight bridges, toll plazas, kid zones and rail crossings, and never pass approaching tracks. [A24]
Source: [A24 -> src:rdmv-ct-d:connecticut-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0024]
FACT_ID: sec05-F19 | anchor: A25
Change lanes solely past mirror, shoulder and far lane sweeps in quick glances that keep forward watch, shifting exactly one lane per move. [A25]
Source: [A25 -> src:rdmv-ct-d:connecticut-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0025]
FACT_ID: sec05-F20 | anchor: A25
Pass one car per maneuver after scanning people, narrow bridges and road hazards that could steal the gap. [A25]
Source: [A25 -> src:rdmv-ct-d:connecticut-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0025]
FACT_ID: sec05-F21 | anchor: A25
Fifty five mile per hour passes eat ten seconds and sixteen hundred feet, a third of a mile, against deceptively still oncoming cars, so doubt means wait. [A25]
Source: [A25 -> src:rdmv-ct-d:connecticut-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0025]
FACT_ID: sec05-F22 | anchor: A25
Reenter only on self found room once both passed headlights fill the rearview, expecting zero courtesy space. [A25]
Source: [A25 -> src:rdmv-ct-d:connecticut-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0025]
FACT_ID: sec05-F23 | anchor: A25
Skip passes at crossings, rails and lot mouths where views die and right turners ignore the lane, and never use any shoulder. [A25]
Source: [A25 -> src:rdmv-ct-d:connecticut-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0025]
FACT_ID: sec05-F24 | anchor: A25
Reserve left lanes for overtakes, keep right under three lanes except passes, left turns and left exits, and signal each shift. [A25]
Source: [A25 -> src:rdmv-ct-d:connecticut-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0025]
FACT_ID: sec05-F25 | anchor: A25
Turn nearest lane to nearest lane along direct paths that cross minimal traffic and no lines, then shift later only with looks and signals. [A25]
Source: [A25 -> src:rdmv-ct-d:connecticut-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0025]
FACT_ID: sec05-F26 | anchor: A26
Swing right turns tight without left feints, cut lefts wide enough for opposing lefts, hold multi turn lanes, and yield turning bikes their rightful road without post pass hooks. [A26]
Source: [A26 -> src:rdmv-ct-d:connecticut-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0026]
FACT_ID: sec05-F27 | anchor: A26
Backing bans travel lanes except parking and K turns, so missed exits mean circling onward, and needed reverses want walk arounds, right shoulder gazes, creeping pace, mirror pauses and spotters. [A26]
Source: [A26 -> src:rdmv-ct-d:connecticut-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0026]
FACT_ID: sec05-F28 | anchor: A26
Light up whenever sight dims, demand a third mile or ten seconds of view, treat blind hills like oncoming cars with no close passes, and mirror downhills for runaway heavies. [A26]
Source: [A26 -> src:rdmv-ct-d:connecticut-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0026]
FACT_ID: sec05-F29 | anchor: A26
Expect the unseen: blocked corner drivers, blind backers, frosted windshields, umbrella walkers and parked car leapers all deserve extra berth. [A26]
Source: [A26 -> src:rdmv-ct-d:connecticut-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0026]
FACT_ID: sec05-F30 | anchor: A26
Never map read rolling, never plug both ears, and never rubberneck crashes, since each steals eyes from braking traffic and breeds new wrecks. [A26]
Source: [A26 -> src:rdmv-ct-d:connecticut-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0026]
